text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx + gateway timeouts observed across gateway-prod (region-us). Error rate spike started ~T-3m. Top signals: 502/504 surge, backend timeouts, and increased origin latency. Investigating prefix-cache layer (kv-prefix-store).
ashley: paging samir (oncall) — looks like multiple clients seeing 5xx, some timeouts trending to 10s+. metrics: 5xx rate x6, p99 latency x3. grafana: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/gw-errors
samir (oncall): on it. initial quick checks: gateway logs show repeated failures when resolving prefix keys — lots of "prefix-unmarshal-failed" and "kv-get-timeout" entries. Going to tail runtime logs.
samir (oncall): running quick checks:
```
# tail last 200 lines for the error
kubectl logs -l app=gateway -n prod --tail=200 | grep -E "prefix-unmarshal-failed|kv-get-timeout" | wc -l
# check kv client errors
ssh cache-ctrl-1 "grep 'kv-get-timeout' /var/log/kv-client/*.log | tail -n 50"
```
ops-bot: metric alert -> kv_prefix_eviction_rate increased from 20/s to 420/s on shard cluster-c-7 in us-west-2. Prefetch latency for prefix keys also increased.
maria (cs): hearing from 2 customers on slack -> elevated error rates on embeddings endpoint, some seeing 502 on POST /v1/generate. CS asks for scope: how many tenants impacted and ETA to mitigate?
samir (oncall): quick scope: preliminary impact estimate ~2.1% of total requests, but concentrated on heavy prefix traffic (many few-tenants). Will confirm exact tenant list shortly.
leo: I see a config change 35m ago to prefetch window size on cluster-c-7 (rollout id: r-2026-11). Could be related.
ashley: good catch. If prefetch window increased we might be thrashing KV memory and causing eviction cascade -> evict hot prefixes -> more origin lookups -> higher latency -> timeouts.
samir (oncall): mitigation plan (live):
- rollback prefetch window to previous value on cluster-c-7 (r-2026-10) — immediate
- enable cache bypass for affected prefix ranges to avoid expensive unmarshalling while we verify integrity
- put short-term circuit-breaker (10m) on cache read path for heavy clients
- take a human snapshot of current KV metrics and begin targeted shard inspection
jordan: runbook link: https://docs.redwood/runbooks/cache-corruption. Steps I'm taking now:
```
# rollback rollout
./deployctl rollback --rollout r-2026-11 --cluster cluster-c-7
# temporarily mark prefixes to bypass
curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/cache/mark_bypass -d '{"cluster":"c-7","prefixes":["pref:tenant:*","pref:hot:*"]}'
```
samir (oncall): executing rollback now. will monitor error rate -> rolling back in waves to avoid a big ripple.
ops-bot: deploy rollback start acknowledged (job id job-9832). Traffic shift will take ~45s per pod batch.
samir (oncall): after initial rollback batch: gateway 5xx trending down from +600rpm -> +120rpm. p95 reduced. Still seeing some corrupt-unmarshal errors though; probably a small set of keys with bad payloads.
maria (cs): pinging affected customers with a brief note. Short message approved: "We are investigating elevated errors for generation endpoints in US-West and have applied mitigations; updates to follow." I'll post to the incident channel in 10m.
ashley: next step: identify and quarantine corrupted prefix keys to stop repeated failing unmarshalls. Prefer surgical key tombstone rather than mass purge.
samir (oncall): steps to locate bad keys:
```
# find recent unmarshal failures and extract key ids
grep "prefix-unmarshal-failed" /var/log/kv-client/*.log | tail -n 200 | awk -F"key=" '{print $2}' | cut -d' ' -f1 | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -n 50
# inspect a sample key payload
ssh cache-node-12 "kvtool dump-key --cluster c-7 --key 'pref:tenant:abc123' | head -n 200"
```
leo: I found ~12 key ids with malformed payloads on c-7. Looks like a partial write or proto version mismatch. We can tombstone those keys and force read-through to origin for them.
jordan: doing tombstone on the suspect keys now (surgical). Command:
```
kv-admin --cluster c-7 --tombstone 'pref:tenant:abc123' 'pref:hot:xyz987' ...
```
ops-bot: tombstone requests accepted. Tombstoning 12 keys on c-7.
samir (oncall): monitoring: errors for that prefix group dropped to baseline within 90s after tombstone + rollback. Overall 5xx rate back to ~1.2x baseline. Still watching p99 latency for a final drop.
maria (cs): update to customers posted. Two tenants with heavy load asked for follow-up postmortem.
ashley: action items for follow-up (create tickets):
- ENG-RUNTIME: root cause analysis for partial writes / proto mismatch on c-7
- ORCH: verify rollout r-2026-11 rollout strategy and canary safeguards
- SRE: add alert for "prefix-unmarshal-failed" spikes and auto-suppress aggressive prefetch config changes
- CS: customer outreach + impact summary for top 10 tenants
samir (oncall): creating handoff note for Jordan (next oncall). Will include timeline, affected tenants, mitigations, and links to logs/grafana. Handoff ETA in 15m.
jordan: acknowledge — I'll take over monitoring and the follow-up RCA coordination. My immediate next steps:
- keep cache bypass active for 30m
- validate there are no remaining corrupted keys beyond the 12 tombstoned
- run a background integrity sweep on cluster-c-7 (non-blocking)
samir (oncall): handing off. brief summary for handoff message:
"Impact: transient spike of 502/504 and timeouts affecting ~2.1% traffic concentrated on prefix-heavy tenants in us-west-2. Root cause: combination of prefetch config change (r-2026-11) that increased memory pressure and surfaced a small set of malformed prefix key payloads causing repeated unmarshal failures and evictions. Mitigation: rollback prefetch change, tombstone 12 corrupted keys, enable short bypass and circuit-breaker; 5xx and p99 reduced to acceptable levels. Next steps: RCA, stronger canarying for prefetch rollouts, alerting, and customer postmortem."
jordan: noted. I'll publish the handoff message and create ENG-RUNTIME ticket with priority P1. tagging @eng-runtime @platform.
ashley: thanks team. once Jordan confirms stable for 30m, I'll close the incident and coordinate a postmortem. Great job moving quickly and keeping CS looped in. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident status -> MONITORING. Tagging oncall handoff to jordan. Incident record: IR-2026-042. Postmortem owner: ENG-RUNTIME assigned. Logs/grafana/links: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/gw-errors | https://logs.redwood/prod/ir/IR-2026-042
jordan: starting monitoring window now. will update in 20m or sooner if anything changes.
